facts: tvOS's WebDriverAgent runner answers from the foreground and stays there, so after a daemon restart it was in front and every press went to it; Mobium now presses Home once when the session opens, only while the runner is in front.

A tvOS alert opens with focus on its cancel button and is answered with the remote: the D-pad moves focus along its buttons, select presses the one with focus, and Back (the remote's Menu) answers with the cancel button.
app_alert accept and dismiss are refused on an Apple TV before anything is sent: WebDriverAgent's accept left the alert up.
note: 296 and 298 as gold, checked against the code (mobiumdriver/alerts.go AnswerAlert refuses on w.tv() before sending; errTVAlert names the D-pad). Added SETUP 'An Apple TV simulator', which says accept and dismiss are refused and how an alert is answered. Since #195, app_alert's button is refused on a TV too (it taps, and noTouch refuses every tap), but that is past the corpus pin. Stored answer muddles the two halves; 298 itself is clear.

findings.what: On an Apple TV, a dialog of three or more buttons is refused with the remedy 'app_alert with button set to one of them' — and button taps the node, which a TV refuses (no touch screen). A remedy that cannot work (CLAUDE.md rule). Unmeasured: MobiumTV's alert has two buttons.
findings.evidence: alert.go:184 WithRemedy("app_alert with button set to one of them, by its caption or its position from 1"); pressAlertButton → s.driver.Tap (alert.go:248) → w3c.pointerSequence returns noTouch on tvOS (w3c.go:161, wda.go:101).

findings.what: app_alert's description says button presses one 'on any dialog', and the CLI example says 'any dialog'; on an Apple TV every button press is refused, and the description never mentions a TV.
findings.evidence: schema.go:1290 "its caption or its position from 1**, on any dialog, an app's own included"; SETUP.md:516 says only accept and dismiss are refused on an Apple TV.
